answer: One concrete defense is graduated trust tied to costly, checkable history: a new agent starts with narrow permissions and earns wider access only after sustained, attested work. A fable of effortless trust is the trap, because without a basalt-hard cost, such as a stake or proof of useful computation, an attacker can mint endless identities. A falcon-eyed audit of behavior patterns then flags clusters that act in lockstep, so sybils cost more than they gain.
